Predict survival curves for a fit

Source: R/methods.R
survkit_curve.Rd

Backend-aware predictions over a time grid for one or more covariate profiles. Parametric, spline and cure fits use the backend's own distribution function and support every type; Cox-family and non-parametric fits use survival::survfit() and support the survival curve.

Usage

survkit_curve(
  fit,
  newdata = NULL,
  times = NULL,
  type = c("survival", "hazard", "cumhaz", "quantile")
)

Arguments

fit

A survkit_fit.

newdata

A data frame of covariate profiles. The default is the backend's reference profile.

times

Numeric times at which to evaluate. The default is an automatic grid from the backend.

type

Character quantity to predict: "survival" (default), "hazard", "cumhaz" or "quantile". The last three need a parametric, spline or cure fit.

Value

A data frame with time, value (named for type when returned by the backend) and a profile index.

See also

survkit_tidy() for the coefficient table, survkit_rmst() for the restricted mean.

Other fit-methods: survkit_tidy()

Examples

fit <- survkit(survival::Surv(time, status) ~ age, survival::lung, method = "weibull")
head(survkit_curve(fit, times = c(100, 300, 500)))
#>   time     value profile
#> 1  100 0.8594618       1
#> 2  300 0.5250282       1
#> 3  500 0.2827438       1
